items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: He called you “Gitch?” ... Yeah “Gitch.” I don’t know where he got that from. That was always “Gitch.”

ctx.x: Yeah “Gitch.” I don’t know where he got that from. That was always “Gitch.” He says, “Kid I have to let you go.” I says, “Why? Am I not good enough?” He says, “No, you don’t belong to the union and you can’t work a steady job until you are here for six months.” They went into the Commodore Hotel and that’s when they had to let me go. And then I moved around, lounged around 48th Street. Musicians were up and down the street and the cops would say, “Come on guys, break it up, break it up.” And one thing led to…
Did you ever consider any other kind of work?
